title: NATO can remain popular while permission for U.S. leadership is divided
source_unit: Pew Research Center 2026 survey of adults in 37 countries, including 13 NATO member states in the alliance-favorability comparison
geography: United States and 36 comparison countries; U.S. partisan estimates and cross-national NATO-member comparisons

nato_member_median_favorability.value: 65% favorable and 30% unfavorable median across 13 NATO member states surveyed

us_partisan_nato_favorability.value: 75% of Democrats and Democratic leaners favorable versus 42% of Republicans and Republican leaners

us_leader_confidence_split.value: 69% of Democrats versus 34% of Republicans confident in Zelenskyy; confidence in Putin was 7% versus 14%

country_counterexample.value: 59% unfavorable opinion of NATO in both Greece and Turkey

institutional_to_action_conversion.unit: willingness to fund, host, deploy, accept risk, change policy, or sustain a specific alliance commitment

observations.method: Pew Research Center survey of nationally representative adult populations in 37 countries, fielded February 8-May 13, 2026; the report presents country estimates, a median across 13 NATO member states, U.S. partisan comparisons, and leader-confidence measures.
observations.uncertainty: Attitudes are measured at one field period and are not behavior. Country medians are not pooled individual-level estimates. Partisan differences may reflect party identity, leader evaluations, ideology, war preferences, question wording, or material interests; the report does not identify the causal source of the gap.
observations.subgroup: U.S. Democrats and Democratic leaners, Republicans and Republican leaners, adults in 13 NATO member states, and adults in 37 surveyed countries; age and ideological comparisons are reported separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may support NATO as a security institution while opposing a specific U.S. administration, war, budget, base, or operation. Unfavorable opinion in one country may coexist with treaty compliance or operational cooperation, and favorable opinion may not survive a future cost or risk.

related_sources.claim: Pew's prior U.S. survey supplies a comparison point for NATO favorability and partisan differences.
Pew documents the survey field period, country coverage, and sampling approach.

boundary: This record adds current public legitimacy and relational-trust measures around NATO. It does not establish alliance operation, defense burden sharing, host-country consent, strategic success, willingness to bear risk, later political action, or durable alignment.
